fields.value: Fashionable and accomplished, with an air shaped by social confidence and aspiration.
Polished, competitive, class-conscious, observant, and capable of calculated civility.
To strengthen her social position, discourage Jane’s connection to Bingley, and attract Darcy.
Bingley’s unmarried sister, educated at a fashionable seminary and proud of a fortune derived from trade.
Social antagonist who amplifies class prejudice and attempts to obstruct both central courtships.
Sister of Charles Bingley and Louisa Hurst.
Moves between Netherfield and London with her family.
Her efforts to diminish Elizabeth sharpen Darcy’s attention; she eventually resumes civility to preserve access to Pemberley.
Darcy: desired match. Elizabeth: rival and target of criticism. Jane: outward friend whose hopes she quietly discourages. Bingley: brother she influences.
